## Summary

Recorded February 5, this wrap contrasts violent silver and crypto moves with software disruption fears. Eisman introduces new Charter and Meritage positions based on future capex relief, buybacks and possible operating improvement, then examines AI spending and several earnings reports.

The Charter and Meritage theses are unusually explicit about their operating mechanisms, but their multiyear forecasts remain unfinished. Charter later results weaken the early stabilization narrative. The capex-versus-cash distinction is useful; high free-cash-flow yield is not a mathematical bankruptcy signal, and less capex does not directly raise current accounting EPS.

<a id="youtube-DoGSH0uTsiM-c014"></a>
### 014. Free cash flow yield equals free cash flow per share divided by the share price.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 10:00-10:12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DoGSH0uTsiM&t=600s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The definition is correct when numerator and denominator refer to consistent equity claims and periods. Forward yield is an estimate.

Conditional reasoning: FCF yield = total FCF/equity market value = FCF per share/price per share.

Assessment test: Use a consistent FCF definition and fully diluted share count.


<a id="youtube-DoGSH0uTsiM-c015"></a>
### 015. A free-cash-flow yield above 20% means investors price a company for bankruptcy.

**Wrong** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 10:10-10:24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DoGSH0uTsiM&t=610s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

A high yield can reflect expected cash-flow decline, capital needs, discount rates or a temporarily high numerator. No yield threshold uniquely identifies bankruptcy expectations.

Conditional reasoning: A temporary FCF of 25 and equity price of 100 yields 25% even if later FCF is lower but positive and the company has no debt. Bankruptcy is not implied.

Assessment test: Model sustainable cash flow, debt service and risk separately.

### 044. If venture investors stop providing cash, OpenAI is finished.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 22:17-22:32](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DoGSH0uTsiM&t=1337s) | Stance: conditional | Horizon: not stated

A continuing cash deficit must be financed or reduced, but stopping one funding source does not logically imply immediate extinction. Debt, strategic funding, restructuring, asset sales or spending cuts are possible.

Conditional reasoning: Loss of one cash source forces adjustment when liquidity is exhausted; it does not alone rule out every adjustment that preserves the firm.

Assessment test: Specify liquidity runway, unavoidable obligations and available alternative capital.

## Framework and tools

- A low multiple needs an operating or capital-allocation catalyst.
- Separate capital spending from earnings and cash generation.
- Watch how competitive narratives change the reaction to good results.
- Distinguish a profitable incumbent funding AI from a loss-making firm dependent on new capital.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Free cash flow per share and yield
- Forward EPS and P/E
- Capex schedules and share repurchases
- Broadband, mobile and video subscriber changes
- Tangible book value
- Hyperscaler capex and cash flow
- Memory supply allocation
